name: 4-[2-(4-hydroxy-3-methylphenyl)propan-2-yl]-2-methylphenol ("Bisphenol C\, dimethyl variant")
note: CAUTION (confirmed by follow-up literature agent, see eralpha_literature_check.csv): PubChem's canonical "Bisphenol C" (CID 6620, this row) is the dimethyl-substituted congener, CAS 79-97-0. It has NO published ERalpha data. The compound EDC toxicology actually calls BPC -- crystallized with ERalpha, ~410x more potent than BPA (Liu et al. 2021 PLOS ONE 16(2):e0246583) -- is CAS 14868-03-2, a dichloro-vinylidene-bridged structure, not this one. A third, again different, ring-chlorinated propane-bridged compound (3,3'-dichloro-BPA) appears in Kitamura et al. 2005 Toxicol Sci. None of the three share a structure; do not conflate them.
